sights.name: Kemuriyama Sunflower Park (next to Kemuriyama Park)
sights.description: Sunflowers are planted in a 2 hectare field in the former Yanshan Nursery, located on the east side of the prefectural forestry technology center, next to Yanshan Forest Park.

sights.name: Mizube no Sato
sights.description: The approximately 1.4km promenade takes advantage of the rich natural forest and clear streams that spread along the Iwasaki River, and includes a suspension bridge, watermill, arbor, and a natural habitat for skunk cabbage.

sights.name: Tokutan Castle Ruins
sights.description: An ancient castle fence built by the conquering shogun Bunshiro Watamaro in the early Heian period (around 813).

sights.name: Mt. Nanshozan
sights.description: At an altitude of 848m, it has been worshiped as a mountain where the dragon god lives in the mountains since ancient times, and you can still see the lion head dedicated to praying for rain on the mountaintop.

sights.name: Jonaiyama Observation Deck
sights.description: Mt. Jonai is 328m above sea level.

sights.name: Denen Hall (Yahaba Town Cultural Center)
sights.description: It was built in 1990 as the prefecture's first music hall. It has a seating capacity of 808 people, with four seats for the disabled, six seats for mothers and children, and headphones for the hard of hearing.

sights.name: Zasukan / Denpoji Temple Ruins
sights.description: There is a small mountain called Zashukan at the foot of the mountain in the western part of the town, and it is said that there was a castle there, but the owner of the castle is unknown.

sights.name: Kemuriyama Dam
sights.description: An earthen dam with a height of 23 meters that dammed the Iwasaki River, which often caused floods and other water damage.

sights.name: Kojin Beach
sights.description: A beach with emerald green water and white sand at the southernmost tip of the Funakoshi Peninsula.

sights.name: Uranohama Beach
sights.description: The beach is shallow and the waves are calm. Nearby are the "Oyster House" and the "Whale and Sea Science Museum" for family fun.

sights.name: Sanriku Yamada Oyster Hut
sights.description: Usually from November to June, Sanriku Yamada Oyster House offers steamed and grilled oysters with a 40-minute time limit.

sights.name: Business Inn Yamada
sights.description: The first business hotel in Yamada Town. All rooms are equipped with a unit bath and toilet.

sights.name: Osawa Garyu Plum Tree
sights.description: Designated as a natural monument by Iwate Prefecture. The tree is approximately 300 years old.

sights.name: Mt. Kujira
sights.description: Kujirayama is located overlooking the Namiita coast and is 610m above sea level.

sights.name: Whale and Sea Science Museum
sights.description: The Whale and Sea Science Museum aims to introduce the mysterious ocean from various angles and deepen visitors' interest in the ocean.

sights.name: Yamada Bay
sights.description: Yamada Bay is almost circular, with a circumference of about 30 km, and the sea surface resembles a calm circular mirror, and the white rock surface and bright green pine trees on the large and small islands make it seem like a large miniature garden.

sights.name: Sekiguchi Fudoson Gorge
sights.description: The Sekiguchi River, which flows under Sekiguchi Fudoson, the inner shrine of Sekiguchi Shrine, has its water source in the virgin forest of Yamamomori.

sights.name: Tabu no Oshima Island

sights.name: Toyomane River Headwaters
sights.description: About 10km upstream from Hito Bridge, deep in the Osonoera swamp, there is a limestone cave that is still not fully understood, and a forest of beech and oak trees that are about 150 years old.

sights.name: Holland Island
sights.description: It is so called because a Dutch ship that was in trouble once stopped here.

sights.name: Shijuhachizaka Observation Deck
sights.description: It was named "Shijuhachizaka" because it was said to be a difficult place for transportation in the past and had many winding slopes.

sights.name: Yamada Senbei
sights.description: Yamada raw rice crackers are characterized by their soft texture, and the more you chew, the more the sweetness and sesame flavor spreads in your mouth.
